title: Personal Credit Cards: Threshold and Cash Value of a Points Statement Credit
content:
This page states when a Personal Credit Cards statement credit from points is made at all, and what it is worth.

## Rule

- No statement credit is made when the card owes nothing or stands in credit.
- No statement credit is made when the number of points to be applied is below the tier's smallest redemption.
- In every other case the credit is made with the points to be applied, and its dollar value comes from pricing those points at the tier's cash worth for each point, with half a cent or more rounding up to the next cent.

## Truth table

| Card owes more than zero | Points to be applied reach the tier's smallest redemption | Statement credit |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | made, for those points |
| yes | no | not made |
| no | any | not made |

## Worked cases (hypothetical; a smallest redemption of 3000 points is assumed purely for illustration)

- Points to be applied of 21437 on a card owing money: the credit is made for 21437 points.
- Points to be applied of 2950: below the assumed 3000, so nothing is credited.
- A card whose amount owed is already below zero: nothing is credited, whatever points it holds.
